text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping has died aged 92 and attention has shifted to his chosen successor, Jiang Zemin.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong praised Deng as one of the world's great leaders in the second half of the century.
- Singapore's non-oil domestic exports fell 3.1 percent year on year in January -- the third consecutive monthly fall -- but economists said the drop was no cause for alarm.
- Aviation industry chiefs in India called for an end to state protectionism coupled with measures in next week's budget to boost overseas investor confidence in the sector.
- Singapore property group Wing Tai Holdings spent Singapore $28.2 million on a 10.73 percent stake in Hongkong-based Winsor Properties.
- Asia's financial markets shrugged off the death of China paramount leader Deng Xiaoping with shares rebounding well from early jitters and currencies left largely untouched.
- Bre-X Minerals Ltd said it would consider merger offers at the right price but the company is focusing on developing Busang, the richest gold find this century.

- The managing director of Australian property group Ipoh Ltd said its major asset, the Queen Victoria Building, could be put into a propery trust along with several prime retail sites to seek outside investors and eventually go public.
